questions.q: Why does the Board's Tableau deck need a different formatting pass than the Executive's Power BI dashboard, even though both read the same warehouse?
options: Power BI doesn't support custom number formatting
Tableau and Power BI require entirely different underlying numbers
The Board is viewed briefly by a mostly non-technical, partly external audience, while the Executive dashboard is clicked through live by someone who lives in the numbers daily
There is no real difference and both should be formatted identically
questions.explain: A board deck gets looked at for a few seconds, not interrogated — it needs to read correctly at a glance, which is a different bar than an Executive's exploratory dashboard.

questions.q: Why are raw warehouse field names like LineTotal and TerritoryGroup renamed before presenting this deck to the Board?
options: Because the warehouse schema itself needs to be renamed too
Because renaming a field changes its underlying calculation
Because warehouse column names are exactly right for a SQL query but exactly wrong for how a board room reads a chart
Because Tableau cannot display field names longer than 10 characters
questions.explain: Plain-language labels like 'Total Sales' and 'Region' read correctly for a non-technical audience, unlike raw column names.

questions.q: Why does this lesson round currency values to something like "$2.4M" instead of showing full precision like "$2,401,983.17"?
options: Tableau cannot store numbers with more than two decimal places
Rounding is required before any number can be exported to PDF
Full precision numbers are factually incorrect
Extra digits of precision actively work against quick reading for an audience glancing at a chart briefly, without changing the underlying number's correctness
questions.explain: The number itself stays correct — this is purely a readability choice suited to a brief, non-interactive viewing.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a worksheet titled "Total Sales by Region" and one titled "Pacific Carries the Quarter"?
options: The first just names what's on screen, while the second gives the board member the headline conclusion before they've finished reading the chart
Only the first title is allowed in Tableau Public
There is no real difference; both are equally good titles
The second title is factually incorrect by definition
questions.explain: A board deck benefits from titles that state a conclusion, since the audience is being told something rather than actively exploring the data themselves.

questions.q: Why can a dashboard be "technically correct" and still fail at being board-ready?
options: Because technical correctness and board-readiness are the same thing by definition
Because board-ready dashboards are never technically correct
Because every number can be accurate while a confusing label, title, or format still causes a board member to walk away with the wrong conclusion
Because Tableau automatically introduces errors when formatting is applied
questions.explain: This lesson doesn't touch a single number — it's entirely about whether the audience reads the already-correct data correctly, which is a distinct skill from building the chart.
